fixtures.basis: Dayton's Building Codes page lists the 2024 Ohio Building Code and 2024 Ohio Plumbing Code with no local amendments, and its FAQ says it uses the codes adopted by the Ohio Board of Building Standards for commercial structures. State law (ORC 3781.01, state pack) allows a municipality only regulations not in conflict with the Board's rules. No Dayton amendment to the toilet counts was found; Chapter 153 of the Dayton code on Municode could not be opened. The state pack's counts stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: When don't I need a building permit? Permits are not needed for painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. The building codes do not require a permit for routine maintenance or minor repairs; however, the work may need to be done by a City of Dayton licensed contractor. If you have any questions as to whether the work you are considering requires a permit or a City of Dayton licensed contractor, please call us at 937-333-3883.
permit.required_quote_city: When do I need a building permit? Building permits are typically required for: All new buildings Any additions to or modifications to existing buildings Any new or modifications to electrical, plumbing or HVAC [...] Call 937-333-3883 if you have specific questions.
permit.state_exempt_list_quote: 102.10 Work exempt from approval. Approval is not required for the following work; however, this work is still to comply with all applicable provisions of the rules of the board: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed one hundred twenty square feet (11.15 m2) and playground structures. 2. Fences not over seven feet (1829 mm) high. 3. Retaining walls which are not over four feet (1219 mm) in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding Class I, II or III-A liquids. 4. Water tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not exceed five thousand gallons (18 927 L) and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed two to one. 5. Sidewalks, parking lots and driveways not more than thirty inches (762 mm) above grade and not over any basement or story below and which are not part of an accessible route. 6. Finishes not regulated by this code, decorating, or other work defined as maintenance or minor repair. 7. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 8. Window awnings supported by an exterior wall of Group R-3. [items 9 to 18: temporary structures and tents, storage tanks, battery smoke alarms, crypts, signs, emergency occupancy] [...] 102.10.2 Minor repairs. Minor repairs to structures may be made without application or notice to the building official. Such repairs are not to include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements; nor do minor repairs include addition to, alteration of, replacement or relocation of any standpipe, water supply, sewer, drainage, drain leader, gas, soil, waste, vent or similar piping, electric wiring or mechanical or other work affecting public health or general safety.
permit.state_required_quote: 105.1 Approvals required. Any owner or owner's representative who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, or change the occupancy of a building or structure, or portion thereof [...] is to first make application to the building official and obtain the required approval.
permit.note: Dayton's FAQ gives its own short list (painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work; routine maintenance or minor repairs). Toilet partitions or compartments are not named there or in the state list (Ohio Building Code 102.10, re-read today on codes.ohio.gov). The state pack shows the code regulates toilet partitions as interior finish (HDPE fire test), so neither list settles a replacement. The FAQ is general (it sits in the 'Permit Process' category, not the commercial one); the commercial FAQ has no partition or restroom item.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Dayton job sites. Price your restroom, choose a material and see the Ohio rules Dayton enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Dayton offices, schools, hospitals and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Ohio's statewide building rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Dayton enforces them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Dayton says building permits are typically required for any modification to an existing building. Its list of work that needs no permit covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, plus routine maintenance and minor repairs. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the Dayton Division of Building Inspection at 937-333-3883 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Dayton Division of Building Inspection
page.install_rule: Dayton registers plumbing, heating and electrical contractors, and says that even work that needs no permit may have to be done by a City of Dayton licensed contractor. Its pages don't say whether that covers partition installation, so ask the Division of Building Inspection. Ohio licenses only five commercial trades at state level: electrical, HVAC, hydronics, plumbing and refrigeration. Partition installation isn't one of them. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Ask the Dayton Division of Building Inspection whether your job needs a City of Dayton licensed contractor.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county and city projects over $250,000 for new construction or $75,000 for remodeling, Ohio law requires at least the wage the state sets for each trade in each county; school district projects are exempt from that law. The state publishes its Montgomery County rates on a portal that needs a login. On federally funded building work in Montgomery County, the federal rate for a carpenter is $21.59 an hour plus $5.70 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Dayton: 5.75% state, 1.25% Montgomery County and 0.5% transit authority.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical offices:** stainless steel or phenolic for rooms that are cleaned often, with accessible stalls in every restroom.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Ohio Building Code (OAC 4101:1, 2021 International Building Code with Ohio amendments, effective March 1, 2024, amended October 15, 2025; listed by Dayton as the 2024 Ohio Building Code), Chapter 11 with ICC A117.1-2017 (new construction and additions) and ICC A117.1-2009 (alterations), Section 102.10 for work exempt from approval; Ohio Plumbing Code (OAC 4101:3, 2021 International Plumbing Code with Ohio amendments; listed by Dayton as the 2024 Ohio Plumbing Code); Dayton Revised Code of General Ordinances Chapter 153 (Unified Building Code) for permits and contractor registration; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
